items.title: LINK-HF2: AI wearable monitoring after HF discharge is feasible, but no reduction in rehospitalization in exploratory analysis (HFSA 2026, JACC: Heart Failure)
items.summary: In 171 patients discharged after acute heart failure, 90 days of AI-analysed continuous patch monitoring with clinician alerts reduced AI-detected physiological instability but did not significantly reduce HF rehospitalization in exploratory analyses (16.3% vs 18.7%; HR 0.90, p=0.76) or a composite of unplanned rehospitalization, ED visits and death.
bullets: **LINK-HF2** (JACC: Heart Failure; HFSA 2026): randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint **feasibility trial** at **5 VA medical centres**.
Adults discharged after **acute HF** wore a **multisensor patch** for up to **90 days**; a personalised **AI model** flagged physiological deviations.
Intervention: AI alerts + a **structured clinician response algorithm** vs standard care. **171 analysed** (80 intervention, 91 control).
**Feasible**: median monitoring adherence **72.4%** of days; clinicians responded in a **median of 1 day**.
The intervention arm had **fewer AI-detected instability episodes** (HR 0.76; 0.60-0.97).
Lesson: **detecting risk is not enough**; workflow integration and a trusted, effective response are the barriers.
